summary: Struct round-trip turned integers into floats, lost >2^53 precision, dropped non-object payload/result
note: integers below 2^53 FIXED 0.1.119, in the inbound direction only (a Struct a client sends is stored as a JSON integer, so REST reads 42). The rest is DOCUMENTED, not fixed (wave 9, 2026-10-12): `Job.payload`, `Job.result`, `EnqueueRequest.payload` and `CompleteRequest.result` are `google.protobuf.Struct`, which holds only a JSON object, so over gRPC a non-object payload or result (array, string, number, boolean, null) arrives with the field absent (`json_to_struct` returns None). Every number a worker receives is a double (a REST payload with n = 42 arrives as `42.0` in Python, Go and PHP and as `42` in JavaScript; whole values below 2^53 are exact and safe to convert back) and an integer of 2^53 or more can arrive rounded (9007199254740993 -> 9007199254740992.0); REST keeps both exactly (reproduced against production 0.1.122 on 2026-10-12). Why it stays open: the fix needs new proto fields (e.g. `bytes payload_json` on `EnqueueRequest` and `Job`, a result twin on `Job` and `CompleteRequest`) read by the four SDKs, a cross-repo contract change. Workaround: use REST, or wrap the value in an object and send big integers as strings. Documented in docs/guides/grpc-server.md (Payloads and results are `google.protobuf.Struct`) and dataflows/grpc-rest.md (Struct numbers); pinned by `docs_contract_tests::grpc_struct_limits_are_true_and_documented`

summary: The worker counter trigger was an immediate AFTER trigger that fired before `trigger_update_dependent_jobs` / `trigger_update_workflow_progress`, so a settling transaction locked the job, then the worker row, then the job's dependents: a worker completing a job and a `dependency_mode = 'any'` dependent it was already running at the same instant deadlocked (225 of 300 rounds of a two-session race)
note: found in review before release: the trigger is a `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint trigger, so its counting UPDATE runs at COMMIT and the worker row is the last lock taken (0 of 300 rounds); the `WHEN` clause is still evaluated at the row update; a failure in the counting UPDATE now fails the COMMIT. The same commit makes the gRPC too-large dead-letter expire the lease first so it is not counted as the worker's failure, and takes the status of REST `job.failed` from the transition instead of a read after the commit. Never make the trigger immediate (invariants #40, fence 30). A database that ran the earlier draft needs its `_sqlx_migrations` row for `20261014110000` deleted once. Test: `w8_jobsapi::w8_worker_counter_does_not_deadlock_concurrent_any_mode_completions`, `w8_events::w8_rest_fail_event_status_comes_from_the_transition`

summary: `workflow.completed` / `workflow.failed` are announced at most once: the scheduler claim commits before the events reach the in-memory delivery queue, so an outcome is lost on a restart at that instant, a full or failing delivery queue, a workflow retried within one 10 s pass, or an outcome over an hour old when first seen
note: DESIGN NOTE, documented and left as is: no outcome is ever sent twice (any number of instances), and making it at-least-once needs a durable outbox, not this claim. The guides, OpenAPI and CHANGELOG 0.1.122 list exactly what can be lost and tell consumers to confirm with `GET /workflows/{id}`; every reopen path must null `completed_at` (invariants #41, fence 31)
